evidence_basis: Assembly listings for every routine. Pseudocode is misleading here: the singleton getters consume no stack, so Ghidra attributes the caller's pushes for the following __thiscall to them at 0041dd64, 0041ddc9, 00bd1780 and 00bd17a0.

free_ring.initial_state: head[i] = i * stride; tail[i] = (head[i] - 1) & mask; entry 0's tail is written explicitly as 0x7ffff
free_ring.push_algorithm: Advance tail[class]. While the advanced tail equals head[next], rotate class next forward one slot: if that class is non-empty, swap the carried block into ring[head[next]] and carry the displaced element; then head[next] and tail[next] both advance; walk to the class after it modulo class_count and stop when it wraps to the starting class. Finally ring[tail[last]] = carried block, live_count += 1, high_water = max(high_water, live_count).
free_ring.pop_algorithm: block = ring[tail[class]]; tail[class] = (tail[class] - 1) & mask; live_count -= 1; high_water untouched.

native_string.capacity_policy: block is always length + 1 bytes; capacity is not stored and is never larger than needed
native_string.growth_policy: exact, no geometric growth; a shrink reallocates exactly like a grow
native_string.ownership: single owner, no sharing and no reference counting in this layer; no destructor, owners resize to 0
native_string.aliasing: resize allocates the new block before releasing the old one, so a grow never reads freed storage
native_string.release_size_contract: every release repeats old_length + 1, because that number picks the pool free list
resize_quirks: A request for the length already held returns immediately even when data is null, so resizing a zeroed string to 0 leaves data null.
With preserve set on an empty string the native calls memcpy with a null source and a zero count.
native_string.assign_is_a_constructor: 0041e87a zeroes length and data before resizing, so calling assign on a live string abandons that buffer; it copies length + 1 bytes and rewrites the terminator resize placed.

deviations: The arena carve throws std::bad_alloc where the native has no bounds check at all and would run past the arena.
allocate never returns null; the CRT-backed allocators throw.
memcpy with a zero count and a null source is skipped rather than called.
NativeString has no destructor, matching the native, but is move-only; owners must call release_to.

uncertainties: Nothing establishes who writes 01090aa4 or when; it turns small-block returns into silent drops.
String pool word +0x4 is never written by the constructor and never read by the four routines examined.
2851 release callers against 63 direct allocate callers: most allocation sites reach the arena through a path this packet did not chase.
No teardown examined; 00bd0c30 registers something at construction and neither pool is freed by anything read here.

Whether the ring cascade can lose a block when every class region is full is not established; the loop stops when the walk wraps and then stores into tail[last], which may be a slot another class still owns. The reconstruction reproduces that rather than guarding it.
The 38 (150-class) and 32 (129-class) ring slots past the last region are never addressed by the constructor and are reachable only through the cascade.
